title: rom-weaver weave
description: Schema revision v2 for the distributable patching-workflow definition. It adds a required shared patchBasis rule. Unknown fields are rejected.

patchBasis.description: Shared input basis for patch entries. Entry basis overrides this rule. auto uses checksum inference.

checkStates.description: Named checksum states. References preserve authored state identity without comparing digest values.

rom.description: The input ROM for the patch chain.

patches.description: Ordered patch chain: array order is the apply order. May be empty only when `cheats` is not.

cheats.description: Cheat selections this weave reproduces, in selection order. They are baked into the ROM after the patch chain. Optional: a weave without it is a plain patch recipe.

output.description: Defaults for the final patched output.

checks.description: Expected checksums (algorithm -> lowercase hex) and/or exact byte size.

checksums.description: Map of checksum algorithm to expected lowercase hex digest.

checkState.description: One named checksum state shared by every field that references its id.

id.description: Stable state identity referenced by checksRef fields.

checks.description: The checksums and/or size this state stands for.

patchInput.description: A ROM/member or prior patch/member selector used by input and target fields. This does not change the authored basis declaration.

rom.description: Marks the selector as the weave's ROM source.

member.description: Exact archive member or disc track.

patch.description: Earlier selected patch id whose real output supplies the bytes.

member.description: Exact member selected from the produced patch output.

rom.description: The one ROM the chain starts from: where to get it and how to recognize it. Omit it for a patch-only weave whose user supplies the ROM.

name.description: Expected source ROM filename. A mismatch is advisory; checks and size verify the bytes.

url.description: Download URL for the ROM. Mutually exclusive with path.

path.description: Weave-relative ROM path. Mutually exclusive with url.

member.description: Exact archive member or disc track to patch.

checks.description: Expected checksums and size for the ROM.

checksRef.description: Named expected ROM state. Cannot be combined with checks.

patch.description: One patch step: its source, display metadata, execution selectors, and declared checks. Exactly one of url or path.

optional.description: When true the patch starts deselected.

url.description: Download URL for the patch. Mutually exclusive with path.

path.description: Weave-relative patch path. Mutually exclusive with url.

input.description: Fixed execution input: the exact ROM/member bytes or a named producer's output. Omitted reads the current accumulated result of its target.

target.description: Cumulative execution lane. Omitted uses the legacy ordered lane; a patch target seeds its lane from the producer when first used.

inputChecks.description: Expected pre-apply state when it differs from rom checks.

inputChecksRef.description: Named authored pre-apply state. Cannot be combined with inputChecks.

outputChecks.description: Expected post-apply state when it differs from final output checks.

outputChecksRef.description: Named authored post-apply state. Cannot be combined with outputChecks.

basis.description: Per-entry base or previous override of patchBasis. Omit when it equals the shared rule.

cheat.description: One cheat selection. `id` names the record in the cheat database; `code` is a raw-code snapshot so the entry still applies when the database is absent.

id.description: Cheat database record ID. An exact description is also accepted, so a hand-authored weave can name a cheat the way `cheat list` prints it. Must not be blank.

source.description: Which database the ID belongs to, for example `libretro-database`.

revision.description: The database revision the selection was made against.

description.description: The cheat's description, as the database records it.

code.description: Raw code snapshot, so the entry still applies when the local cheat database is absent.

codeKind.description: Explicit decoder for the raw code snapshot.

optional.description: When true an unresolvable cheat is skipped and named in the report; omitted/false makes it fail the apply.

output.description: Defaults and expected result for the final patched output. Compression stays an apply-time choice.

checks.description: Expected checksums and size after the full chain.

checksRef.description: Named expected final-output state. Cannot be combined with checks.
